Craft.Domain: Provides reusable business-rule contracts, a catalog base for evaluating rules, and violation values that identify the failed rule and affected member.
Craft.Persistence: Defines reusable read, write, and combined repository contracts for persistence providers.
Craft.Persistence.EFCore: Implements the generic Craft repository contracts over an EF Core context. The Smurfs app-data adapter builds its Smurf repository on this implementation.
Smurfs.API: Provides the ASP.NET Core API host with OpenAPI setup and a sample weather forecast endpoint.
Smurfs.Application: Defines the MediatR create and list use cases, their request and result models, and the read-service contract. Create evaluates domain rules and writes through a unit of work. List delegates the paged query to the read service.
Smurfs.Domain: Defines Smurf, Pet, and Village and the domain rules that apply to them. It owns the name validation rule and registers it in the Smurfs business-rule catalog.
Smurfs.Infrastructure: Implements the application's Smurf read service against the app-data EF Core context. It orders, pages, and projects results for the list use case. It also provides the shared Serilog rolling file setup used by the console and WPF.
Smurfs.Persistence: Defines the Smurfs persistence contracts for the Smurf repository, app-data initialization, and unit-of-work creation and lifetime.
Smurfs.Persistence.EFCore.AppData: Stores Smurfs, Pets, and Villages in SQLite through EF Core. It owns the app-data context, mappings, migrations, repository, unit of work, initialization, and seed data.
Smurfs.Persistence.EFCore.Identity: Owns the separate ASP.NET Core Identity store, including the user model, EF Core context, SQLite migrations, and sample-account seeding.
Smurfs.UI.Console: Hosts the command-line interface. It composes the application and persistence services and exposes commands to initialize the app database, create a Smurf, and list Smurfs with paging.
Smurfs.UI.WinForms: Starts a Windows Forms desktop host and opens its initial form.
Smurfs.UI.WPF: Hosts the Windows desktop interface. It composes services at startup and supplies the windows and dialogs for browsing the catalog and creating a Smurf.
Smurfs.ViewModel: Provides the presentation state and commands for the WPF catalog and create dialog. It dispatches application requests through MediatR and exposes results and validation feedback to the views.
Smurf.Persistence.EFCore.AppData.UnitTes: Exercises the app-data EF Core mappings, migrations, repository, and unit of work against isolated SQLite databases. It also verifies that the create handler honors rules from the registered catalog.
